comments.value: Please VRC devs, follow this redesign. this is great, amazing use of space!!!

This is so much better.

The "before" version is very tall, which works on the website where it's easy to scroll, but not ingame where it's more confined. It has way too much empty space and it feels much more difficult to navigate around. Your bio doesn't even show up until the bottom, and it gets cut off way too early. Having the represented group shown under the name feels like a bandaid fix for groups not even appearing until you scroll.

This concept fixes all of that. It does seem a bit strange to put links and languages where you did, but I can't think of anything better.

This is a good way to introduce a scrollable bio that wouldn't interfere with scrolling the whole page since it's off to the left you'd be much less likely to accidentally scroll the bio when trying to scroll the page.
@{65d4c188d003b08e88570818|full_name} yes aiya we like it too

I swear that vrchat is trying too hard to make profiles on platform match closer to discord to help people make the blind "thisisfine.jpg" decision to link their discord account. which, already, is a mondo big security risk as it stands if you don't have 2FA absolutely everywhere. for the standard user, it isn't enabled. VRC should step up and mandate 2FA for everyone if they're going to try and be buddy-buddy with the same instagram execs that mandated the discord UI change and screwed that place over. 

but additionally, the new UI specifically for nameplates is absolutely horrendous. See attached pic.  no one needs to see the banner's group name above someone's head. the banner is now forever messed up on many of them, people who have taken ample steps to properly center their group banners now have to wait for a new template with updated margins... and let's not even get to the point of not being able to immediately spot someone in a crowd because you can't see your friend's highlighted name anymore. this yellow stroke outline is the most inaccessible thing I've ever seen on this platform and feels like we're back in 2021... and I wasn't even on this platform back then. The nameplate system that exists in stable is widely accepted as the norm and this feels like a change in the wrong direction if one wants to keep user count up. 

Accessibility with the new menus is also wack. I had to turn on the setting for reduction of UI motion AGAIN because it was forcibly turned off with the new changes, and the right-click reticle garbage can get booted right out the door. it should *not* be on by default to bring up someone's profile if you right-click on someone with your reticle as a deskie. it's a nice feature I'm sure, but don't turn it on by default to make everyone accidentally trigger it, instead give an update message that explains it instead.
The nameplate design is weird too. The beta version of UI doesn't show the group image properly.
Definitely need to also keep the yellow names. Much easier to find in a crowd

Same color for friend names affects some menus differently and should be looked at again too. Not as easy to distinguish between friends and non-friends in the location 'Here' tab anymore for example, as it's missing the new yellow border.

Could be resolved by just including the yellow friend border in all menus, as shown in mockup below.

Also group banners are kinda weird now, and the other mockup below is just an idea for a different solution.

In addition to the nameplate custom styles like the cube thingy, could just have group banners show up like that. Would eliminate the need for a group banner above the nameplate, outside of the menus. (And would show a represented group in all menus, which seems neat to be honest.)

But it would clash with custom nameplate styles being sold, eh, could be a choice to represent instead of custom style I guess.

In general: the information-density on the new UI is really low compared to old version.  So similar changes to side-wings, and listings as well.

(I know you're thinking "but the nooobs! think of the noobs! when faced with ~50 controls in one menu!"   and the answer is: menu option for information density defaults "low" so you've got your onboarding-shallow-water, switchable to high for bloomberg-terminal-mode.   At several hundreds of friends, and in events, these are super important controls!)

details:
The new profiles contain less information available at first glance, things are all over the place (e.g. pronouns next to Verified 18+ next to represented group), elements appear big. I believe in having more things at glance, no layout shift (things moving other things), better grouped information, less empty space - better effectiveness and readability in short. 

I put together my slightly reimagined version of the design in the attachment that might better convey what could be improved.

2 screenshots - before and after
